title: A remote job charges for useless training
mechanism_summary: An online job advert promises easy earnings from home. Instead of employment, the applicant pays for useless training, certification, or starter materials.
suggested_beats: A flexible job promises easy money.
Starting requires an upfront purchase.
Verify the employer before paying for job access.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone looking for work from home
why_it_works: The prospect of income makes a startup cost seem recoverable.

title: A shipping job recruits an unwitting intermediary
mechanism_summary: A supposed employer hires someone to receive and forward packages. The goods may have been bought with stolen cards, while the promised wage never arrives.
suggested_beats: An online employer offers parcel work.
Repacking hides the original purchase trail.
Treat reshipping job offers as a serious warning sign.
why_it_works: Ordinary shipping tasks can conceal participation in a fraud.

title: A copied rental advert collects a deposit
mechanism_summary: Scammers copy a real rental listing and replace the contact details. Applicants send deposits to someone who cannot provide the property.
suggested_beats: A convincing rental advert attracts interest.
The contact demands money before verification.
Verify the property and landlord independently.
why_it_works: A plausible listing and housing pressure can overwhelm verification.

title: Recovery help starts with another advance fee
mechanism_summary: Someone contacts a person who already lost money and promises recovery. The supposed helper demands an upfront payment, causing another loss.
suggested_beats: A past scam victim is offered help.
Recovery requires paying first.
Verify recovery claims before sending more money.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone trying to recover a previous loss
why_it_works: Hope of reversing a loss makes another payment feel justified.

title: A caller offers a refund for fake technical support
mechanism_summary: A supposed support provider says a refund is available. The refund story is used to request financial information or access rather than return money.
suggested_beats: A caller offers an unexpected refund.
Processing it requires private financial access.
Contact the original provider independently.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone who previously bought technical support
why_it_works: The prospect of reimbursement makes renewed contact seem welcome.

title: An online directory call becomes a bill
mechanism_summary: A caller offers to confirm a business listing or provide free advertising. Later the business receives a charge for something it did not knowingly purchase.
suggested_beats: A caller requests routine listing details.
A supposedly free interaction becomes an invoice.
Verify any claimed advertising agreement.
why_it_works: Routine information checks can be misrepresented as purchase consent.

title: A bargain supplier never provides the goods
mechanism_summary: A supposed work opportunity asks someone to buy discounted luxury goods for resale. After payment, the goods never arrive or prove worthless.
suggested_beats: A seller promises easy resale profit.
The purchased stock is missing or worthless.
Research the supplier before committing money.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone hoping to start a resale business
why_it_works: The promised margin makes an unverified supplier look like an opportunity.

title: A mystery-shopping assignment diverts money
mechanism_summary: A supposed employer sends a mystery-shopping check. The worker is told to transfer some funds onward before the check is discovered to be fake.
suggested_beats: An assignment arrives with a check.
The task requires forwarding money.
A deposited check is not proof that funds are genuine.
why_it_works: An apparent test assignment disguises a transfer to the scammer.
